drug_class: Combined Hormonal Oral Contraceptive (Birth Control Pill)
purpose: This medication is used to prevent pregnancy. It may also be prescribed to help regulate your menstrual cycle, reduce menstrual cramps, or treat acne in some cases. Your doctor may also use it to manage certain hormone-related conditions.
how_it_works: This pill contains two hormones — a progestin (levonorgestrel) and an estrogen (ethinyl estradiol) — that work together to prevent pregnancy. They mainly work by stopping your ovaries from releasing an egg each month. They also thicken the mucus in your cervix so sperm have a harder time getting through, and they thin the lining of your uterus so a fertilized egg is less likely to attach.
common_side_effects: Some people experience nausea, breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, spotting or breakthrough bleeding between periods, mood changes, or decreased sex drive. These side effects are often mild and tend to improve after the first few months of use.
warnings: This medication is not recommended if you smoke and are over 35 years old, as it raises the risk of serious blood clots, stroke, or heart attack. Tell your doctor if you have a history of blood clots, high blood pressure, migraines with aura, liver problems, or certain cancers. This pill does NOT protect against sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Stop taking it and call your doctor right away if you experience severe chest pain, sudden vision changes, severe headache, or leg pain or swelling.
typical_dosing: You usually take one pill by mouth at the same time every day. Depending on the specific pill pack you have, you may take active hormone pills for 21 days followed by 7 reminder pills, or follow a different schedule such as 84 days of active pills. Try to take it at the same time each day — setting a daily alarm can help you remember. Missing pills can reduce effectiveness, so follow the instructions in your package carefully.
